title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
abstract: arXiv:2610.14209v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. A third option is to have cloud models write a program that devices execute: the data stays local, but as the program is written before any data is seen, it fails whenever a step depends on interpreting content that appears only at run time. We explore an intermediate architecture, in which the cloud-written program defers bounded questions over user data to a small local model through an ordinary function call. On AppWorld this improves the success rate of a code-only agent in all six combinations of backbone model and test partition we evaluate, by up to 14.9pp, recovering a substantial part of the gap to a cloud-hosted ReAct loop while keeping user data on the device.

translated_title: 小语言模型应该坐上驾驶座吗？关于本地模型作为云端编写的智能体程序解释器的研究
translated_abstract: 执行用户所提供任务的最准确的智能体由大型云端托管模型驱动，这些模型通过读取用户的私人数据来完成任务。由足够小、可在边缘设备上运行的模型驱动的智能体能够将数据保留在本地，但效果要差得多。第三种选择是让云端模型编写一个由设备执行的程序：数据保持在本地，但由于程序是在看到任何数据之前编写的，因此当某个步骤依赖于解释仅在运行时出现的内容时，程序就会失败。我们探索了一种中间架构，其中云端编写的程序通过普通函数调用，将对用户数据的有限问题委托给小型本地模型处理。在 AppWorld 基准上，这一方法使我们评估的所有六种骨干模型与测试分区组合下纯代码智能体的成功率均得到提升，最高提升 14.9 个百分点，在保持用户数据留在设备上的同时，大幅缩小了与云端托管的 ReAct 循环之间的性能差距。
tldr: 该论文提出一种混合架构：云端模型编写的智能体程序通过普通函数调用，将涉及用户数据的有限问题转交给本地小语言模型处理，在保持用户数据本地化的同时，于 AppWorld 基准上将纯代码智能体的成功率最高提升 14.9 个百分点，大幅缩小了与云端 ReAct 智能体之间的性能差距。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a hybrid architecture where cloud-written agent programs delegate bounded questions over user data to a small local model via ordinary function calls, improving a code-only agent's success rate by up to 14.9pp across all six backbone model and test partition combinations on AppWorld, while keeping user data on the device and recovering much of the gap to cloud-hosted ReAct agents.
